# AGENTS.md

Repository instructions for AI coding agents. Keep this file short, concrete, and tied to commands that actually work in this
repo. If a fact here conflicts with source files or CI config, trust the source file and update this guide.

## Project Snapshot

Memos is a self-hosted note-taking app.

- Backend: Go 1.26.2, Echo v5, Connect RPC, gRPC-Gateway, Protocol Buffers.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, React Query v5.
- Storage: SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.
- Generated API outputs: `proto/gen/` for Go/OpenAPI, `web/src/types/proto/` for TypeScript.

## Working Rules

- Read relevant code before editing; prefer local patterns over new abstractions.
- Keep diffs scoped. Do not do repo-wide cleanup, dependency churn, or generated-file rewrites unless the task requires it.
- Do not hand-edit generated proto outputs. Change `.proto` files, then run `buf generate`.
- Add migrations for all database drivers when schema changes, and update each driver's `LATEST.sql`.
- Add public API endpoints to `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`.
- Ask before adding heavy dependencies, changing auth/token behavior, or altering Docker/release workflows.

## Commands

Run from the repository root unless a command starts with `cd`.

```bash
# Backend
go run ./cmd/memos --port 8081    # Start backend dev server
go test ./...                      # Run all Go tests
go test -v ./store/...             # Store tests, including DB drivers via TestContainers
go test -v -race ./server/...      # Server tests with race detector
go test -v -race ./internal/...    # Internal package tests with race detector
go test -v -run TestFoo ./pkg/...  # Run matching Go tests
go mod tidy -go=1.26.2             # Match CI tidy check
golangci-lint run                  # Go lint, config: .golangci.yaml
golangci-lint run --fix            # Auto-fix lint, including goimports

# Frontend
cd web && pnpm install             # Install dependencies
cd web && pnpm dev                 # Dev server on :3001, proxying API to :8081
cd web && pnpm lint                # Type check + Biome lint
cd web && pnpm test                # Vitest unit tests
cd web && pnpm build               # Production build
cd web && pnpm release             # Build SPA into server/router/frontend/dist

# Protocol Buffers
cd proto && buf generate           # Regenerate Go + TypeScript + OpenAPI
cd proto && buf lint               # Lint proto files
cd proto && buf format -w          # Format proto files
```

## Code Map

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/memos/main.go` | Cobra/Viper CLI setup and server startup |
| `server/server.go` | Echo HTTP server and background runner wiring |
| `server/auth/` | JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, PAT handling |
| `server/router/api/v1/` | Connect/gRPC-Gateway services, ACL config, SSE hub |
| `server/router/frontend/` | Static SPA serving |
| `server/router/fileserver/` | Native HTTP file serving, thumbnails, range requests |
| `server/runner/` | Background memo processing and S3 presign refresh |
| `store/` | Store facade, cache, migrations, driver interface |
| `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/` | Database-specific drivers and SQL |
| `proto/api/v1/` | Public API service definitions |
| `proto/store/` | Internal storage proto messages |
| `internal/` | App-private packages: scheduler, cron, email, CEL filter, markdown, idp, S3 |
| `web/src/connect.ts` | Connect RPC clients, auth interceptor, access-token refresh |
| `web/src/auth-state.ts` | Token storage and BroadcastChannel cross-tab sync |
| `web/src/hooks/` | React Query hooks for server state |
| `web/src/contexts/` | React context for client/UI state |
| `web/src/components/` | Radix/Tailwind UI components and feature components |
| `web/src/themes/` | CSS themes using OKLch color tokens |

## Change Routing

| Change | Update | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go service or router behavior | Service code under `server/`, tests near package | `go test -v -race ./server/...` |
| Store or migration behavior | `store/`, all three DB driver migrations, `LATEST.sql` | `go test -v ./store/...` |
| Internal package logic | Relevant `internal/` package tests | `go test -v -race ./internal/...` |
| Frontend behavior | Components/hooks/contexts under `web/src/` | `cd web && pnpm lint && pnpm test` |
| Frontend production output | Vite config or release-sensitive UI | `cd web && pnpm build` or `pnpm release` |
| Proto API | `.proto` source plus generated outputs | `cd proto && buf generate && buf lint` |
| Public unauthenticated route | `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` | Targeted server test or manual route check |

## Go Conventions

- Wrap errors with `errors.Wrap(err, "context")` from `github.com/pkg/errors`; do not use `fmt.Errorf`.
- Return service errors with `status.Errorf(codes.X, "message")`.
- Keep imports grouped as stdlib, third-party, then `github.com/usememos/memos`; goimports is run by golangci-lint.
- Add doc comments for exported identifiers; godot enforces exported comment punctuation.
- Avoid package-level mutable state unless the surrounding package already uses that pattern.

## Frontend Conventions

- Use `@/` for absolute imports.
- Follow Biome formatting: 2-space indent, double quotes, semicolons, 140-character line width.

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

Memos is currently a `0.x` project. Security fixes are only provided for the latest release. Older releases are not supported for security updates, and fixes are not backported.

If you run Memos in production, keep your instance updated to the latest release.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Please report security issues privately by email: `dev@usememos.com`

Do not open public GitHub issues, discussions, or pull requests for suspected vulnerabilities.

Please include:

- A clear description of the issue
- Steps to reproduce
- Affected version or commit
- Deployment details that matter to reproduction
- Your assessment of impact

We will review reports as time permits and fix valid issues in regular releases.

## Disclosure and CVEs

Memos is self-hosted software and is still in the `0.x` stage. At this stage, we do not run a formal disclosure program, publish separate security advisories for every issue, or request CVE IDs.

Security fixes may be shipped directly in normal releases or noted briefly in release notes and changelogs.

## Self-Hosted Deployment Notes

The security posture of a Memos instance depends heavily on how it is deployed and operated. In particular:

- Keep Memos updated
- Put it behind a properly configured reverse proxy when exposed to the internet
- Require authentication for any non-public deployment
- Use TLS in production
- Limit access to trusted users and administrators

Reports that depend entirely on intentionally unsafe deployment choices, unsupported local patches, or administrator actions may be treated as deployment issues rather than product vulnerabilities.

The goal is to identify multiple independent server surfaces that enforce memo visibility, rather than a single centralized check.

Five server surfaces enforce memo visibility independently. These are the API v1 router, file server, RSS router, frontend sitemap, and SSE hub. MCP is not an independent enforcement site.

API v1 GetMemo/ListMemos — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go
File server attachments — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
RSS feeds — server/router/rss/rss.go
Frontend sitemap — server/router/frontend/frontend.go
SSE event delivery — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go

Reconsidering whether "enforcement site" means individual functions rather than entire routers. GetMemoByShare bypasses visibility checks entirely. Need to verify whether webhook dispatch or the runner also enforce visibility, and examine memo_service_query.go.

`checkMemoReadAccess` is the dedicated helper for memo read access, but many server surfaces re-implement the check inline instead of calling it.

Five distinct enforcement sites were identified:

- API v1 memo service (`checkMemoReadAccess` + ListMemos)
- File server (attachments inherit memo visibility)
- RSS (public only)
- Frontend sitemap (public only)
- SSE hub (event fan-out)

Seven distinct enforcement sites were identified across the codebase. These include `checkMemoReadAccess` in `memo_service.go`, `canViewerAccessMemo` in `user_service_notifications.go` and `notification/email.go`, `canUserAccessMentionContext` in `memo_mention_helpers.go`, `canReceive` in `sse_hub.go`, `checkAttachmentAccess` in `attachment_service.go`, and `checkAttachmentPermission` in `fileserver.go`.

Query-level enforcement also appears in `ListMemoComments` (`memo_service_comments.go`), `ListMemoRelations` (`memo_relation_service.go`), `batchConvertMemoRelations` (`memo_service_converter.go`), and `GetUserStats` / `ListAllUserStats` (`user_service_stats.go`). Inline single-memo checks appear in `ListMemoAttachments` (`memo_attachment_service.go`) and `ListMemoReactions` (`reaction_service.go`).

Comment and reaction write permissions are excluded because the question concerns viewing only. The final list of distinct enforcement sites for viewing includes `GetMemo`, `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, `ListMemoAttachments`, `ListMemoReactions`, `ListMemoRelations`, `GetAttachment`, the file server, RSS, the sitemap, the SSE hub, `GetUserStats`, and notifications.

A stricter definition of "viewing a memo" excludes attachments, stats, and notifications. Under this interpretation, only `GetMemo` and `ListMemos` in `memo_service.go` enforce visibility on the memo itself. `GetMemoByShare` uses share tokens without checking memo visibility.

The sitemap is weak enforcement because it only generates URLs rather than gating content. The "at least three" hint suggests listing every distinct server surface, including ListMemoComments and relation snippets, rather than stopping at the core memo endpoints. Client-side visibility checks are excluded since the question asks for server surfaces.

Notifications and email are excluded because they control notification delivery rather than viewing access. The final list narrows to distinct request-handling packages that enforce visibility directly on served content.

The store layer merely applies the VisibilityList provided by its callers; it does not enforce viewer checks itself. The three primary enforcement sites are the API service layer, the file server, and RSS. The frontend sitemap and SSE hub are treated as secondary extras.

ListMemoRelations does not check the parent memo's visibility. It only filters related memos by visibility. This makes it a weaker enforcement site than ListMemoComments, which validates the parent memo itself.

The answer is being narrowed to the three primary router surfaces and named policy functions that enforce view access. A gap in ListMemoRelations was noted but set aside.

Stats are included because they aggregate viewable memos under the same viewer filter. The answer is being refined to the most precise list of distinct enforcement sites.

Notification and email access checks are now included as enforcement sites, since they literally evaluate whether a viewer may access a memo using the visibility field. The final list is being compiled as distinct functions and sites.

The final list is being finalized. It includes the sitemap, SSE hub, user stats, and notification/email helpers. The author is weighing whether to list every distinct enforcement site or only the three primary router surfaces.

The author is settling on a middle-ground approach. Distinct server surfaces and their primary enforcement files will be listed. API duplicates that merely call a shared helper will be grouped together. Files that independently implement the viewing policy will be enumerated separately.

Write-side permission checks such as CreateMemoComment are excluded because they govern commenting, not viewing. The final answer will be compact, using function names where available and descriptive labels otherwise.

The author is grouping API endpoints by surface rather than enumerating every inline duplicate. The planned answer structures enforcement sites by router surface: the memo service, attachment service, memo attachment service, reaction service, and memo relation service.

Webhooks, the ACL layer, and MCP were ruled out as enforcement sites. The ACL layer delegates visibility filtering to the service layer. MCP reuses the API surface. The author is now considering whether to limit the answer to only the three router packages that independently query memos with VisibilityList: the API memo service, RSS, and frontend.

The final answer will list every distinct enforcement site as one line per file. Multiple checks within the same file are merged into a single site. The first entry is `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` for `checkMemoReadAccess` and `ListMemos`.

The author has finalized the eleven enforcement sites. They span the API v1 router layer, covering memo comments, attachments, reactions, relations, stats, SSE, notifications, and mentions.
